name: PUMA
verdict: Being rated: a maintainer decides whether an NGO investigation of forced-labour indicators at Taiwanese textile suppliers connected to its supply chain counts as a finding against the company.
note: Rating note: Deal signed Jan 2026 and cleared by Chinese and Indian competition authorities; completion by the time of writing is assumed but not separately confirmed. On hold for a maintainer (same question as Rodd & Gunn): Transparentem's report 'Following the Thread: Labor Abuses in Taiwan's Textile Industry' (published February 2025, transparentem.org/report/taiwan-following-the-thread/) investigated more than 90 migrant workers at nine Taiwanese textile suppliers and found evidence of conditions the ILO defines as indicators of forced labor, including recruitment fees as high as $6,000; Puma is listed among the buyers contacted in March 2024 with possible supply-chain connections (a remediation group leader), and audits commissioned by buyers broadly confirmed the findings. The reported abuse is at deeper-tier suppliers, not by PUMA itself, and no court or regulator finding against PUMA was found. On state ownership: the HKEX filing does not identify ANTA's own controlling shareholders; ANTA has no known material state stake - worth revisiting if a state fund takes a position.
